task.description: CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR (WF-02 Step 1b) re-check of REQ-157's design after rework commit 3680243, which was intended to fix section 4.4's install/2 fold and section 6.1's raise expression, previously FAILed for containing literal Elixir code bodies instead of prose/type-shape descriptions.

checks_performed.section_4_4_rework: PASS -- section 4.4's install/2 description no longer contains any Elixir code block. The former illustrative `Lua.set!(lua, [:platform, row.name], fn args -> Capabilities.check!(...); row.stub.(args) end)` expression has been replaced by a 4-step numbered prose description of required wrapper behavior (resolve row, apply row.required, call Capabilities.check!/3, invoke row.stub on success), explicitly labelled 'a description of required behavior, not an Elixir expression.' Confirmed via `git show 3680243 -- lib/letflow/design/req157-lua-capability-model.md`.
checks_performed.section_6_1_rework: PASS -- section 6.1's raise description no longer contains a literal `raise Lua.RuntimeException, scope: ..., ...` expression. It is now a 5-row table naming each keyword-list key (:scope, :function, :message, :capability_required, :capabilities_granted), its value/derivation, and whether the library validates it, explicitly labelled 'a description of the required shape, not an Elixir expression.'
checks_performed.regression_skim: PASS -- `git show 3680243 --stat` confirms only lib/letflow/design/req157-lua-capability-model.md (54 lines changed: 37 insertions, 23 deletions) and the step-01-code-designer.json handoff were touched by the rework commit; the diff is confined to sections 4.4 and 6.1 exactly as scoped. Full skim of the rest of the document (sections 1-3, 4.1-4.3, 5, 7-12) shows no other content changed: all 8 AC mappings (section 7), the capability matrix (4.1), service_capability/1 (2.5), the now/fail ungated moduledoc requirement (5), cross-module dependency table (8), test suite spec (9), invariants (10), and open questions (11) are byte-identical to the previously-passed version.

new_issue_found_not_part_of_rework_scope.no_implementation_code_present: FAIL. Section 4.3 (unchanged by this rework, pre-existing since the original design commit 19abb6a) states: "`now`'s matrix row's `stub` is literally `fn _args -> [Platform.now()] end`, the same closure REQ-152's `install/1` already built inline." This is a real, syntactically valid Elixir anonymous-function expression presented as literal fact ('is literally'), not a signature, @spec, or type shape -- the same category of violation that failed sections 4.4 and 6.1 in the prior pass. It was not flagged in the prior FAIL verdict (which enumerated exactly two violations and did not mention this line), but its presence in the document now under re-review is a genuine, current violation of WF-02 Step 1b(e)'s 'no actual .ex/.exs code blocks -- signatures and type shapes only, not bodies' rule. Per this role's mandate ('FAIL immediately and completely on any single failed check -- no partial credit'; 'don't approve a design because it's close enough'), a design containing a real code snippet cannot pass regardless of whether an earlier review pass missed it.

issues: lib/letflow/design/req157-lua-capability-model.md section 4.3, the `:now` stub bullet: replace `fn _args -> [Platform.now()] end` with a prose description (e.g. "the `now` stub is the same zero-argument wrapper around `Platform.now/0` that REQ-152's `install/1` already builds inline, returning a one-element Lua return list -- not a new closure, just relocated into the fold's per-row stub slot") -- do not restate the closure literal itself. Re-check the rest of section 4.3 and the whole document one more time for any other literal code fragments outside @spec/@type blocks (which are permitted) before resubmitting.
